utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm Dr Sharma. Thanks for coming in — and you're right to book it urgently, that must be uncomfortable. Tell me, what's been going on since yesterday? Is it just the burning, or have you been needing to go a lot more often or more urgently too?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago. It stings and burns, and it is worst right at the end of going to the toilet. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out and I have to rush. It is also a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

reply: No fevers or shivers, and I haven't been sick and am eating normally. I don't have anything in my back, just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy.

utterance:
Here's what I've found and my plan. Your urine test shows signs of infection — lots of white cells and nitrites — and your urine pregnancy test is negative, so I'm confident this is a simple bladder infection (cystitis). Importantly, you don't have fever, back pain or tummy signs that would suggest the infection has spread to the kidneys, so it's treatable as an uncomplicated infection.

I've prescribed nitrofurantoin — one 100 mg capsule twice a day for 5 days. Please take them with food, and finish the whole course even if you feel better sooner. It doesn't interact with your pill.

A few practical tips:
- Drink plenty of water over the next few days and try not to hold on to wee, especially at work.
- You can take paracetamol or ibuprofen for the burning and tummy ache.
- The symptoms usually start improving within 24–48 hours.

One important thing: come back or call us sooner if you develop a fever or shivers, pain in your back under your ribs, nausea or vomiting, blood in your wee, or if you're not better after 48–72 hours — that could mean the infection has moved up and you'd need different treatment. And if you get these symptoms again, or two or more times in the next six months, book in so we can look at prevention options. Any questions?
reply: That's great, thank you so much for the script. I've got to get back to my shift at the café now.
